newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT - India GDRs slip despite Bombay rise.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT - India GDRs slip despite Bombay rise.

text.p: Indian global depository receipts (GDRs) eased on Monday, failing to reflect local market strength amid a lack of follow through support, traders said.
They said buying had appeared in selected stocks early on, but limited interest later in the day and concern about short term prospects in Bombay had weighed on prices.
"The market is cautiously optimistic. But there is some nervousness with some long positions being squared," a trader said.
He said early demand was seen for Reliance and SBI, but the market lacked further support.
SBI added 43 cents to $21.35/22.00 and Reliance shed 25 cents to $17.00/18.00.

The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR index closed 0.24 points lower. The index finished 0.32 percent down at 75.79, while the premium over the local market slipped to 16.56 percent from 18.80 percent on Friday.
The Bombay Stock Exchange 30 share index added 52.81 points to 3,798.12.

In other Asian markets, the Capel Taiwan GDR Index ended up 4.79 points at 116.26. Prices were at a 0.37 percent premium to the local market from a 0.16 percent discount on Friday. The local market made 1.63 percent on Monday.
The Capel Korea GDR Index ended 3.71 percent higher at 58.80, a 2.10 point rise. The premium was 44.10 percent.
